items.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998
items.q: Coltrane was just a name to me, I’d never even heard him

ctx.x: Do you suppose that performance, and especially that introduction was completely spontaneous?

No I don’t think so. I never talked to Louis about that, but I’m sure — man as I get older I get hoarser talking, talking — I’m sure that he had a pattern worked out, just as you can hear in the many, many performances of things that he did constantly in performances, broadcasts and so forth. The British trumpet player Humphrey Lyttelton wrote a very good piece many years ago about the people who say oh he just plays the same solo over and over again. And he pointed out that he certainly does not and he cited…

When you were doing this research in your early years of listening, did you start in your mind to be able to categorize things? Like when you heard something did you think of it as New Orleans jazz or Chicago style, or was there a difference between black and white bands for instance that you could hear?
